proposal: Show this story's summary, authored facts and attached lore together in Scene details.
current: Native Summarize, World Info and Vector Storage exist; the scene inspector does not consolidate them.
preserve: Native summary, lore and retrieval owners; distinguish visible summaries from underlying recall.
acceptance: Opening or correcting memory preserves transcript, draft, focus and story identity. Show coverage and stale/unavailable states. Never convert character replies into user drafts.

proposal: Add a readable explanation of the context used for a selected reply, with expert detail available.
current: Native client-side itemization and prompt manager exist. Backend compatibility post-processing can change messages before the provider call. Inclusion/exclusion reasons may need native-owner instrumentation.
preserve: Native client assembly, backend compatibility processing, recorded generation identity and explicit settings. Provider-side chat templates remain a separate visibility boundary.
acceptance: Label recorded client assembly, recorded compatibility processing and unavailable provider-side stages. Never present reconstructed content as a captured final provider request. Show model, budget and available contributions without inference or remounting chat.

proposal: Present existing branches and checkpoints as navigable story relationships.
current: Native branch and bookmark operations exist; workspace story rows are a flat conversation list.
preserve: Native transcript files, swipe selection, integrity and full character/group identity.
acceptance: Create/open a branch at an earlier saved reply; the original file, selected reply and draft remain intact. Mobile ancestry navigation stays usable at 448px.

proposal: Show whether an edit affects this story, the reusable character, a preset or a service connection.
current: Native character, preset and service scopes exist. A chat-specific scenario override already exists in public/script.js:9064–9113. Complete isolated scenario snapshots are not established.
preserve: Current native persistence semantics; do not create an override store to make labels look consistent.
acceptance: Explain the actual affected scope before save/apply. Switching stories proves that story-only changes do not become shared character/provider changes.

proposal: Lead creation with identity, premise and opening; keep full native fields reachable as detail.
current: Native character editor and imports remain available. Workspace profiles already separate premise, opening and full description.
preserve: Character-card fields, metadata, import/export, alternate greetings and advanced controls.
acceptance: A minimal card can start a story without a required title or a mandatory multi-step wizard. Existing detailed cards retain every field.

proposal: Offer optional scenario/opening choices beside Start new story and clearly distinguish a new scene from continuation.
current: Immediate start, premise preview, exact-history continuation, alternate greetings and a native chat-specific scenario override already exist. A reusable scenario library or full isolated scenario snapshot needs separate verification.
preserve: One-click default start, native automatic names and no mandatory title prompt.
acceptance: Default start remains immediate. Optional suggestions require an explicit request, can be cancelled, and never replace the saved character or silently consume inference.

proposal: Make edit, retry, continue and alternative selection easier to discover while explaining how they affect history.
current: Native message editing, swipes, generation and branch operations exist.
preserve: Native event ancestry and generation cancellation; expert generation controls remain available.
acceptance: Touch and keyboard can find each action. Retry preserves alternatives; destructive rewind and branch have distinct consequences. Menus dismiss outside without losing the draft.

proposal: Show effective service settings and an optional per-service test beside connection choices.
current: One-server discovery, native service settings, context discovery, failure/retry and optional writer already exist.
preserve: Native keys, profiles, exact model IDs, explicit overrides and optional services; no new registry or protocol proxy.
acceptance: Separate discovery success from successful generation. Explicit tests disclose that they send a request, can Stop, and never change a model policy or story selection.

proposal: Explain export scope and make ordinary backup/export easy before a service or device move.
current: Native character/chat/lore exports exist. Complete branch/media/preset round-trip fidelity is not established by current browser acceptance.
preserve: Standard formats, original files and privacy; export must not imply automatic sharing.
acceptance: Distinguish selected text, structured story, character and complete backup. Report included/excluded variants, media and hidden context. Test synthetic round trips before promising lossless migration.

proposal: Keep active speaker, turn mode and shared scene context close to group chat.
current: Native group member, activation and reply-order controls already exist and are linked from Scene details.
preserve: Native cast scheduler and shared versus individual memory boundaries.
acceptance: Manual and automatic turns remain distinguishable. Stop ends the queue; changing a speaker never changes the saved character or another story's context.

proposal: Make it easy to revisit a story's images and voice settings from its messages.
current: Native media/gallery and voice mapping exist; manual image and opt-in narration controls are already near chat.
preserve: Native media storage, per-character mapping and audio opt-in.
acceptance: Image selection returns to the originating message. Service or voice changes show their scope. No automatic microphone or continuous call is introduced.

proposal: Retain the mounted conversation and predictable transient controls when the tab returns.
current: Actual release has synthetic desktop/Pixel hidden-freeze, draft, history-position, portrait and menu regressions. Physical phone locking remains unqualified.
classification: Existing behavior to preserve; physical validation gap
preserve: Native replies, scroll ownership, drafts, optional audio and explicit retry.
acceptance: No reply-recovery popup, replayed inference, portrait overlap or cut-off final line. Test a physical Pixel 9 Pro XL separately before claiming lock/GPU qualification.
